DILG Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 116 s. 2021 SEP 29 2021 VICE-MAYOR SOLFERINO A. AGRA, JR. Municipality of Claveria Province of Cagayan Dear Vice-Mayor Agra: This refers to your undated letter referring to the DILG Secretary, for appropriate action, the alleged refusal of elected Mayor Celia Layus (hereinafter referred to as "Mayor Layus") to recognize your automatic assumption as Acting Mayor of Claveria since she is still claiming herself able to work despite her sickly condition and long continued absences in office. Based on your letter, hereunder are the relevant factual antecedents: • • On November 13, 2019, Mayor Layus suffered a stroke that caused her to undergo immediate medical treatment; Thereafter, Mayor Layus returned to work on December 23, 2019; However, at noon of that same day, she filed another sick leave for 20 days accordingly for medical check-up but returned to work again after a few days, long before the applied period has lapsed; According to you, with all of her "back to work" written declaration to the Sangguniang Bayan, no "certification" was shown that her sickness being the legal cause for her absences in office no longer exists pursuant to Section 46 (b) of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991. You are of the view that this certification is among the legal requirements to a valid resumption to duty; You further manifested that since her stroke on November 13, 2019 up to April 20, 2021 , the Mayor was seen in the Municipal Hall carried on a wheelchair for only five occasions. According to you, with reliable information, Mayor Layus could not speak, react, nor communicate with others per manifestations of various sectors; Sometime in February 2020, you filed a Petition for Que Warranto before the RTC to declare the Mayor in "temporary incapacity" premised with the foregoing circumstances; However, your Petition for Quo Warranto was dismissed for your failure to prove the "permanent incapacity" of Mayor Layus. You are also of the view that the

• Decision dated April 23, 2021 was based on an issue that you never sought for resolution or tried either, Aggrieved, you filed a Motion for Reconsideration before the RTC, which was heard for the first time on August 18, 2021 or over 3 months from its filing; You are of the view that having prevailed in her Quo Warranto case, Mayor Layus is expected since then to report to her office. However, she did not publicly surface even for a single opportunity nor similarly, reported to her office for any undertaking or purpose officially or otherwise; For this, you "automatically" assumed as acting Mayor on July 26, 2021 pursuant to Section 46 (a) in relation to Section 444 (c) and 445 (a)(4) of the Local Government Code of 1991, jurisprudence, DILG Opinion No. 18, series of 2021 and DILG Opinion No. 20, series of 2013. You bolstered your automatic assumption on the following documents: a) SB Resolution No. 093, series of 2021 (August 4, 2021) — "Affirming the automatic assumption of the Honorable Vice Mayor Solferino A. Agra, Jr., MD, as Acting Mayor of the Municipality of Claveria, Cagayan" (Annex A); b) Manifestation-Liga ng mga Barangay Claveria Chapter—"Manifestation with urgent request for the Honorable Vice Mayor to automatically assume as Acting Mayor" (Annex B); c) Manifestation- Officials and Employees (The Mayor has not been publicly seen for almost two (2) years now) (Annex C) Hence, you raised this sole issue for resolution of the Department: "Is the Automatic Assumption of the Vice-Mayor as Acting Mayor valid?" In answering the aforesaid sole issue, we deem it proper to stress several points: First, the position of a Municipal Mayor or local elective offices, in general, are imbued with public interest; it is where the welfare of the public/constituents are of paramount importance. Consequently, local elective officials are expected to discharge their functions proactively, both physically and intellectually. We understand that during their incumbency, local elective officials encounter challenges in health and/or legal constraints which prevent them from discharging proactively their duties and functions. Second, with respect to health challenges, when a local elective official has severe illness during his incumbency, the normal course of things would be for him to either resign or file a leave of absence, whichever he opts to do so, in which case, the rule of succession may now be properly applied, whether referring to permanent or temporary vacancy. Thus, for those times that Mayor Layus has approved applications for leave, you, as Vice-Mayor, are mandated to assume the Office of the Mayor as Acting Mayor. Upon the expiration of her leave of absence, Mayor Layus shall submit to the Sangguniang Bayan a written declaration that she has reported back to office. She

need not submit a "certification" that her sickness no longer exists since under Section 46 (b) the Local Government Code of 1991 , such written declaration would suffice. On the other hand, with regard to legal constraints such as suspension imposed by the Office of the Ombudsman or appropriate local Sanggunian, the normal course of things would be to apply the rule of succession until such time that the suspension ends. The problem, however, would arise in case the incumbent local elective official has severe illness but in his point of view, despite his physical limitation, he can discharge the duties and functions of his office. Thus, he does not resign nor file leave of absence. In the perspective however of others, he can no longer do so. In this situation, there is no permanent or temporary vacancy to speak of and that the rule on permanent vacancy under Section 44 of the Code or the rule on temporary vacancy under Section 46 of the same Code cannot yet be applied. Neither does the Local Government Code empower any agency or official of the government to determine that indeed the severe illness of the incumbent local elective official is sufficient to render him temporarily or permanently incapacitated and subsequently, declare permanent or temporary vacancy in the office. Third the Department is consistent in its position that in cases of severe illness of the incumbent local elective official but does not resign nor file a leave of absence and instead, insists on continuing to hold Office when in the meantime his physical or mental sickness will not allow him—the declaration on whether there exists temporary or permanent vacancy is an adjudicatory matter. This means that the determination on whether the incumbent local elective official is temporarily or permanently incapacitated to discharge the duties and functions of his office on account of severe illness and accordingly, declaration on whether there exists a temporary or permanent vacancy in his office, should be obtained from the Regional Trial Court, a court of general jurisdiction. We note that in this case of Claveria, you actually filed a Special Civil Action for Quo Warranto before RTC-Branch 12 against Mayor Layus praying for a declaration that the latter is already incapacitated to perform her function. Unfortunately, however, RTC- Branch 12 rendered a Decision dismissing your Petition for lack of merit. This only means that Mayor Layus's incapacity to discharge her functions was not proved before the Court. With your failure to get a declaration from RTC-Branch 12, we thus find your assumption to the Office of the Mayor, as Acting Mayor, during those times that Mayor Layus did not file leave of absence, without any basis. May it be respectfully noted that the jurisprudence that you mentioned in your letter namely, Gamboa v. Aguirre (G.R. No. 134213, July 30, 1999), Grapilon v. Municipal Council (112 Phil 29), and Paredes v. Antillon (113 Phil 643) do not apply in the case at hand as they pertain to different set of facts/circumstances. Those cited cases pertain to absence of the mayor due to travel outside of his territorial jurisdiction. On the other hand, DILG Opinion No. 20, series of 2013 also does not pertain to severe illness of the incumbent local elective official. It pertains to the temporary incapacity of the Mayor in Bangued, Abra due to the Warrant of Arrest issued by RTC-Branch 2 (Abra) against the Mayor coupled with his absence and non-performance of his duties and functions. Further, it appears that DILG Opinion No. 18, series of 2021 was

wrongly cited since upon checking, it pertains to the prohibition of a Provincial Legal Officer to handle certain cases. Lastly, aside from seeking a court declaration on whether there exists a temporary or permanent vacancy in the Office of Mayor Layus due to her severe illness, you may also file an administrative case for Dereliction or Neglect of Duty before the Office of the Ombudsman or the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, if there be pieces of evidence showing that she failed to discharge her duty/ies as Mayor of Claveria. When the breach of duty is flagrant and palpable, this may even warrant the supreme penalty of dismissal from the service, which is one of the grounds of permanent vacancy under Section 44 (d) of the Local Government Code of 1991. The Supreme Court defined these offenses in the following cases as follows: I) A.M. No. 17-01-04-SC dated February 7, 2017 Re: Complaint of Aero Engr. Darwin A. Reci against Coutt Administrator Jose Midas P. Marquez and Deputy Coutt Administrator Thelma C. Bahia Relative to Criminal Case No. 02-236956 "Dereliction of duty may be classified as gross or simple neglect of duty or negligence. Gross neglect of duty or gross negligence 'refers to negligence characterized by the want of even slight care, or by acting or omitting to act in a situation where there is a duty to act, not inadvertently but wilfully and intentionally, with a conscious indifference to the consequences, insofar as other persons may be affected. It is the omission of that care that even inattentive and thoughtless men never fail to give to their own property.' It denotes a flagrant and culpable refusal or unwillingness of a person to perform a duty. In cases involving public officials, gross negligence occurs when a breach of duty is flagrant and palpable. In contrast, simple neglect of duty means the failure of an employee or official to give proper attention to a task expected of him or her, signifying a "disregard of a duty resulting from carelessness or indifference." 2) CSC, et al. vs. Catacutan [G.R. No. 224651, July 3, 20191; Catacutan vs. CSC, et al. [G.R. No. 224656] "The gravity of negligence or the character of neglect in the performance of duty is certainly a matter of evidence and will direct the proper sanction to be imposed. On one hand, gross neglect of duty is understood as the failure to give proper attention to a required task or to discharge a duty, characterized by want of even the slightest care, or by conscious Indifference to the consequences insofar as other persons may be affected, or by flagrant and palpable breach of duty.lt is the omission of that care which even inattentive and thoughtless men never fail to give to their own property. In cases involving public officials, there is gross negligence when a breach of duty is flagrant and palpable. Under the law, this offense warrants the supreme penalty of dismissal from service. Simple neglect of duty, on the other hand, is characterized by failure of an employee or official to give proper attention to a task expected of him or her, signifying a disregard of a duty resulting from carelessness or indifference This warrants the penalty of mere suspension from office without pay." It may be recalled that on October 14, 2020, the Civil Service Commission (CSC) adopted Resolution No. 2000912 providing for "Amendment to the Revised Interim Guidelines for Altemative Work Arrangements During the State of Public Health Emergency Due to COVID-19 Pandemic". In Item 3.1 of the aforesaid CSC

Resolution, the parameters in the implementation of Work-from-Home (WFH) arrangement are set as follows: "3.1 Work-from-Home c. Employees who are below 21 years old and those who are 60 years old and above. as well as those with immunodeficiency. comorbidities or other health risk, and pregnant women, and are residing in areas placed under ECQ. MECQ. GCQ and MGCQ shall be under work-from-home arranqement. except when their services are indispensable under the circumstances or when office work is permitted. The said work arrangement shall also be made available to those living with the aforementioned persons and living in area under ECQ, MECQ and GCQ; (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the foregoing, those who are 60 years old and above as well as those with immunodeficiency, comorbidities or other health risk and are residing in areas under ECQ, MECQ, GCQ and MGCQ shall be under a WFH arrangement. Let it be noted however that the aforequoted provision of the CSC Resolution is not absolute as there were exceptions: l. When the services of the employees are indispensable under the circumstances; or 2. When office work is permitted. In these two (2) exceptions, the employees are required to work on site (WOS). It is settled that Mayor Layus is a senior citizen with immunodeficiency, comorbidities or other health risk having been in paralyzed state. Hence, she may claim to work under a WFH arrangement. However, we are of the view that her duties and functions as Mayor of Claveria cannot be discharged in all instances via the WFH arrangement. An example of this is the duty of the Mayor under DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2020-0771 for the local government units (LGUs) to fully establish and activate their respective Local Task Force Against COVID-19 and align all their actions with the national strategy framework. Section 3 of DILG MC No. 2020-077 reads: "3. Policy Content and Guidelines 3.1 A local task force aqainst COVID-19 in every Province, City, and Municipality shall be established by each respective LGU. 3.2 LGUs shall facilitate the establishment of their own Local Emergency Operations Center to enable them to monitor and analyze data coming from the local government and interior sectors. 1 Entitled "RATIONALIZING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT TASK FORCE AGAINST COVIID-19"

This is to better address the concems and issues of their constituents in their respective localities. 3.3 The LGU Task Force shall be composed of, but shall not be limited to, the following. 3.3.1 3.3.2 Head: Local Chief Executive (LCE)- The task force shall be orqanized and headed by the Local Chief Executives of the respective Provinces. Cities. or Municipalities. In gase of vacancy, absence. or incapacity of the LCE. the LGU shall follow the rules on succession under the Local Government Code to determine who shall organize and serve as head of the task force. Members: DILG (C/MLGOO) PNP P/C/MDRRMO MHO BHW BHERT BPSO RESU/LESU Further, in Items 3.6 and 3.9 of DILG MC No. 2020-077, it was stated that: "3.6 The LGU task force shall take the lead in all related situations and concerns. and closely coordinate with the DOH-Center for Health Development. 3.7 Video teleconference CVTC) and other media platforms may. be used for easy coordination/cohesive action." (Emphasis Supplied) Taking into account the foregoing, the establishment and activation of the Municipal Task Force Task Force Against COVID-19 under Item 3.3. I in relation to Item 3.6 of DILG MC No. 2020-077 appear to be functions which cannot be performed under a WFH arrangement. Should Mayor Layus opts to designate another official to organize and head the Municipal Task Force Task Force Against COVID-19 in her stead, then this is a categorical acknowledgment on her part that there is "vacancy, absence or incapacity" in her position as Mayor of Claveria. Note that in Item 3.3.1 of DILG MC No. 2020-077, "vacancy, absence or capacity" were the cited grounds where the Mayor could renounce the position as head of the task force to her successor, who is most likely you. Premises considered, while it is true that there may be instances when the Mayor could discharge her functions under a WFH arrangement, we are of the view that this is not always the case. The establishment of the Municipal Task Force Task Force against COVID-19 as well as taking the lead in all related situations are examples of the Mayor's functions which cannot be performed under a WFH arrangement. Her

failure to organize the Municipal Task Force Task Force against COVID-19 and take the lead in all related situations could be a ground for Dereliction or Neglect of Duty. On a final note, pending court declaration that the position of Mayor Layus is temporarily or permanently vacant, or any finding of guilt for Dereliction/Neglect of Duty, you cannot yet assume to the Office of the Mayor. Otherwise, such assumption is tantamount to "usurpation of authority or official functions" punishable under Article 177 of the Revised Penal Code. This is notwithstanding the adoption of SB resolution No. 093, series of 2021 and manifestations from the Liga ng mga Barangay (Claveria Chapter), and officials and employees therein. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: IRINGAN Unde ecretary for Local Government OUSLG/MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/clp Copy furnished: DIRECTOR JONATHAN PAUL LEUSEN Regional Director, DILG-Region II Regional Government Center Carig Sur, Tuguegarao City Cagayan
